summary: Uther sends for the Duke of Tintagel and his wife Igraine, desires her, and loses her when the two ride home by night; he besieges the duke, falls sick with love, and a knight of his goes to find Merlin.

Merlin gets Uther into Tintagel in the duke's likeness on a promise of the child, the duke is killed that night, Arthur is begotten, Uther marries Igraine, two of her daughters are married to kings, and Morgan le Fay is sent to school.
Igraine learns the king fathered her child, and Merlin carries the newborn from a back gate to the lord chosen to raise him, where he is christened Arthur.
Uther falls sick, is carried in a litter to win a battle, lies speechless, and dies after naming Arthur his heir before the barons.

The realm is without a king until Merlin has the archbishop call the lords to London at Christmas, where a sword stands in a stone for whoever is rightful king, and the boy Arthur pulls it out to bring his foster brother a sword.
Arthur draws the sword again and learns that the man who raised him is not his father; the lords put off the choice from feast to feast as he draws it each time.
At Pentecost the people demand Arthur, who is knighted and crowned, swears to rule justly, gives back lands taken since Uther died, and names his officers.

Twelve elderly envoys of the Roman emperor Lucius demand the tribute Britain once paid to Rome; Arthur shelters them courteously, Cador welcomes a war, and Arthur argues that his forebears ruled Rome, so Rome owes him.

Arthur's allies pledge armies, he sends the envoys back with a claim to the empire, and Lucius, warned of Arthur's might, raises a vast host from across his empire, with fifty giants, and marches into France.
At a parliament in York Arthur assembles his fleet, leaves the realm and Guinevere in the care of Baudwin and Constantine, names Constantine his heir should he die, and sails from Sandwich.

At sea Arthur dreams of a dragon from the west destroying a black boar from the east; a sage reads the dragon as Arthur and the boar as a tyrant or giant he will fight, and the fleet lands at Barfleur.

A countryman tells of a giant on Mont Saint-Michel who has carried off the Duchess of Brittany; Arthur climbs the mount with only Kay and Bedivere waiting below, finds her dead, kills the giant in a wrestling fight, and has a church built there.

Gawain, Bors, Lionel and Bedivere carry Arthur's challenge to Lucius; Gawain beheads a kinsman of the emperor who mocks the Britons, and the envoys fight their way back to their ambush and rout the Romans who pursue them.

Guinevere rides out a-Maying near Westminster with ten knights dressed in green and no armed guard; Meliagaunce, Bagdemagus's son, who has long loved her and feared only Lancelot, lies in wait with men and archers.
Meliagaunce ambushes the queen; her ten unarmored knights kill forty of his men before they fall wounded, and she yields to save them on condition that they stay with her.
Guinevere secretly sends a page with her ring to Lancelot; Meliagaunce sets thirty archers to kill Lancelot's horse but not to fight him, and Lancelot arms and rides out, leaving word for Lavaine.

Lancelot swims the Thames, the archers shoot his horse, and weighed down by his armor he kills a carter and rides in a cart to Meliagaunce's gate, where a lady says he looks bound for the gallows, and he breaks the gate.

Meliagaunce begs the queen's mercy and she makes peace to avoid scandal, calming Lancelot, who is called the Knight of the Cart thereafter; she promises to meet him that night at a barred window, and Lavaine arrives.

Lancelot tears out the window bars, cutting his hand, and spends the night with the queen; in the morning Meliagaunce sees blood on her sheets and accuses her of lying with one of the wounded knights.

Lancelot rebukes Meliagaunce for opening the queen's curtains and takes up his challenge to fight in eight days; showing him the castle, Meliagaunce drops him through a trapdoor into a pit, and the court supposes Lancelot has ridden off.
A lady brings Lancelot food and begs his love, which he refuses; on the day of the fight she frees him for a single kiss and gives him his armor and a white horse.

As Lavaine is about to fight for the queen at the stake, Lancelot arrives and exposes the trap; he strikes Meliagaunce down, the queen signals for his death, and fighting bareheaded with his left arm bound, Lancelot splits Meliagaunce's head.

Mordred forges news of Arthur's death, is crowned at Canterbury, and plans to marry Guinevere, who escapes to the Tower of London and holds it against him; the Archbishop of Canterbury curses him and flees to Glastonbury, and the fickle English rally to Mordred at Dover.
Arthur forces a landing at Dover against Mordred; Gawain, struck on his old wound, dies after writing to beg Lancelot to come and save the king, and Arthur beats Mordred again on Barham Down.

At the parley an adder stings a knight, he draws his sword to kill it, and both hosts charge; by nightfall only Arthur, Lucan and Bedivere are left alive, Arthur runs Mordred through, and Mordred deals him a mortal head wound as he dies.

Lucan dies lifting the king; Bedivere twice hides Excalibur instead of throwing it into the water, then throws it, and a hand catches it; three queens in a barge take Arthur away to Avalon to be healed.
